description:
Enhance the existing ASCII charting module (benchbox/core/visualization/ascii/) with new chart
types and improved comparison visualizations. The current implementation has 6 chart types across
~2,255 lines and is well-architected with terminal capability detection, ANSI color support, and
Unicode fallbacks.

Key enhancements needed:
1. Paired comparison bar chart - side-by-side bars (e.g., SQL vs DataFrame) with inline percentage
   change annotations, regression/improvement color coding, and scale notes
2. Diverging bar chart - centered-zero horizontal bars showing regression/improvement distribution,
   sorted by magnitude, with overflow arrows for outliers
3. Summary box - bordered panel with key aggregate metrics (geo mean, total time, improved/stable/
   regressed counts, worst/best queries)
4. Inline percentage annotations - "+23%", "-57%", "← !" markers alongside bars
5. Intelligent truncation - handle outliers (e.g., Q21 +726%) by truncating bars with indicators
   rather than compressing the entire scale

Library evaluation conclusion: Keep custom implementation. Evaluated 10+ terminal charting libraries
(plotext, plotext-plus, termgraph, plotille, uniplot, rich, textual, asciichartpy, drawille,
bashplotlib). None can replace the existing module without significant adaptation. Key reasons:
- BenchBox needs render() -> str pattern; most libraries print to stdout
- Benchmark-specific features (Pareto frontiers, best/worst markers, grouped multi-platform bars,
  auto-chunking) don't exist in any library
- Sub-character bar precision (1/8 Unicode blocks) exceeds all library implementations
- 4-tier terminal color degradation (truecolor -> 256 -> 16 -> none) with NO_COLOR support is
  more robust than any library
- Zero dependency advantage is significant
Closest competitor was plotext-plus (7/10 fit) but still needs wrappers for string output,
benchmark annotations, and regression highlighting. Full evaluation documented in this item.

anti_patterns.why: the render()->str pattern, benchmark-specific features, and sub-character precision cannot be replicated; custom implementation evaluated as superior to all 10+ candidates

anti_patterns.dont: compress the entire bar scale for outliers
anti_patterns.why: it makes most bars unreadably small; truncate outlier bars instead with overflow indicators
base.py already handles terminal detection; use self.width from ASCIIChartBase
all ASCII charts must return strings for MCP tool responses and CLI piping
ASCII_BLOCK_CHARS and ASCII_BOX_CHARS exist for terminals without Unicode support

preserves.behavior: 4-tier color degradation chain (truecolor -> 256 -> 16 -> none) must work for new chart types
ASCIIChartBase interface and render() -> str contract must not change
ASCIIChartOptions(use_color=False) must produce clean output without ANSI codes for new charts
Existing 6 ASCII chart types (bar, histogram, heatmap, box, line, scatter) must remain fully functional
Factory functions from_bar_data(), from_query_latency_data(), etc. must remain backward-compatible
MCP generate_chart tool must continue to work for existing chart_type values
Unicode -> ASCII fallback must work for all new chart types
